stories.title: Verify recipes transform multiple inputs into multiple outputs over duration
stories.i_want: a building's recipe to consume several distinct inputs and produce several distinct outputs over a fixed duration
stories.so_that: co-product chains like an oil refinery's fuel+bitumen are representable without new engine work

acceptance_criteria.text: A Recipe can declare 2+ input items and 2+ output items simultaneously, each with independent quantities and a shared production duration. [SUBSTRATE: PROVIDED — prototypes/src/types/recipe.rs:35-47]

One building type is bound to exactly one recipe (ADR-0017's W&R shape: a building is its product, not a generic machine with a swappable recipe category). [SUBSTRATE: PROVIDED — GoodsCompanyPrototype.recipe: Option<Recipe>, per docs/adr/0017-a-building-is-its-product.md]

stories.title: Verify extraction buildings produce with no consumed inputs
stories.i_want: a mine or field to output raw material from labour and time alone, consuming no input items
stories.so_that: the base of every supply chain (ore, timber, crops) exists without a phantom input recipe

acceptance_criteria.text: A Recipe with an empty inputs list is valid and produces output at its declared rate whenever labour/power/output-space gates are satisfied. [SUBSTRATE: PROVIDED — base_mod/companies.lua:56]

stories.title: Verify full output storage halts production (the cascade engine)
stories.i_want: a factory to stop producing once its output buffer is full
stories.so_that: a jammed downstream (freight backed up, warehouse full) visibly and physically stalls the factory instead of goods vanishing or piling up unboundedly

acceptance_criteria.text: When a recipe's output storage cannot accept another batch, production halts entirely (rate → 0) until space frees, and resumes automatically once it does. [SUBSTRATE: PROVIDED — recipe_should_produce, souls/goods_company.rs:36-39]

stories.title: Verify declared workforce is sourced live from present population, not stockpiled
stories.i_want: a factory's WORKERS_NEEDED figure to be satisfied by whichever citizens are actually present and working that tick
stories.so_that: labour behaves as a physical, non-storable input rather than an inventory the player can bank

acceptance_criteria.text: Workforce sourcing is computed per-tick from n_workers present at the building, never drawn from a stored labour stock. [SUBSTRATE: PROVIDED — goods_company.rs:25,266-295]

stories.title: Verify production never checks the treasury before running
stories.i_want: production to run purely on physical availability (labour, power, inputs, output space)
stories.so_that: the game's one rule holds: nothing is produced merely because money is available, and nothing is blocked merely because money is short

acceptance_criteria.text: No internal recipe execution path reads or checks Money/treasury balance; production gates are exclusively physical factors. [SUBSTRATE: PROVIDED — internal recipes never touch Money, per audit §3]

stories.title: Scale output continuously with staffing fraction, not linearly
stories.i_want: understaffed factories to lose output along the diminishing-returns curve the spec adopts, not a flat linear ratio
stories.so_that: partial staffing behaves like the reference model (full staffing + full power + no iron = no steel; the curve, not just presence/absence, communicates how badly understaffed a factory is)

acceptance_criteria.text: Today's labour factor is workers_present/workers_needed applied linearly. [SUBSTRATE: PARTIAL — souls/goods_company.rs (labour scaling is linear, per audit §3)]

The labour factor must instead follow the adopted curve rate = 2·e − 200·e/(staffFrac+100) (e = worker efficiency), producing a strictly smaller output than the linear model at all staffing fractions strictly between 0 and 1. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield, curve not implemented; spec adopts CS1's PrivateBuildingAI.cs:397]
At staffFrac = 0 the labour factor is 0 (zero workers → zero output) and at staffFrac = 1 it is 1 (full staffing → no labour penalty). [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield curve boundary condition]

A recipe may opt out of per-worker rate scaling and declare its production rate as a whole-building constant unaffected by staffFrac curve math — the documented water-well exception — while every other recipe still applies the per-worker curve from AC-2. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield; spec/production.md:32 (water_well_*.ini exception)]

stories.title: Throttle output continuously with available power instead of a binary blackout gate
stories.i_want: a brownout (partial power deficit) to reduce a factory's output proportionally rather than the plant running at full rate until power fails, then dropping to zero
stories.so_that: power reads as a graduated physical constraint the player can manage (shed load, prioritize feeds) rather than an on/off trap

acceptance_criteria.text: Today power is a binary gate: any network blackout stops output entirely; there is no partial-power state. [SUBSTRATE: PARTIAL — souls/goods_company.rs:95-101, binary blackout gate]

f_power must scale continuously with electricity_available (0..1), matching W&R's CONSUMPTION_PER_SECOND gating-input model: at partial availability output is throttled proportionally, not merely on or off. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield continuous power factor]

Idle-draw fallback: a factory not currently producing due to another gate still draws a reduced power fraction (idle-vs-producing modal ~0.4) rather than zero or full draw. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield, W&R ELETRIC_WITHOUT_WORKING_FACTOR token]

A separate lighting-off power draw fraction (distinct from the idle-vs-producing fallback in AC-3) reduces a factory's power draw when its lighting is disabled, independent of whether it is currently producing. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield; spec/production.md:58 ($ELETRIC_WITHOUT_LIGHTING_FACTOR)]

stories.title: Throttle output continuously with scarcest input stock instead of an all-or-nothing stall
stories.i_want: a factory running low on one input to slow down proportionally to that input's remaining stock, not run at full rate until the input hits zero
stories.so_that: the scarcest-factor bottleneck (Liebig's law) reads as a rate decay the player can see coming, not a cliff

acceptance_criteria.text: Today recipe_should_produce is a boolean stall: production runs at full rate while every input is above its threshold and stops entirely the tick an input hits zero. [SUBSTRATE: PARTIAL — recipe_should_produce is a bare bool, souls/goods_company.rs]

f_inputs must become min over all inputs of (available/required), each input independently throttling the rate to its own stock fraction; a single input at zero drives f_inputs (and thus output) to exactly 0. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield, spec adopts CS1's ProcessingFacilityAI.cs:471 per-input throttle]
Two inputs at different stock fractions (e.g. 80% and 30% of required) yield a rate bounded by the lower (30%) factor, not the higher or an average. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield min() semantics]

stories.title: Combine all production factors multiplicatively so the scarcest factor wins
stories.i_want: the realized output rate to be the product of every independent factor (labour × power × inputs × machinery × water), not the minimum of any single one
stories.so_that: compounding deficiencies compound their effect exactly as physical causality demands — full staffing and full power cannot compensate for a half-supplied input

acceptance_criteria.text: output_rate = base_rate × f_labour × f_power × f_inputs × f_machinery × f_water_quality × f_output_space, where each f_x ∈ [0,1]; the final rate equals the arithmetic product of all factor values, not their minimum. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield; today the composed multiplicative formula does not exist, only the independent binary/boolean/linear gates cited above]
Any single factor at 0 drives the composed rate to exactly 0 regardless of the other factors' values (full staffing + full power + zero iron = zero steel). [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield]

stories.title: Surface the active bottleneck reason to the player
stories.i_want: to see, per stalled or throttled factory, which single factor (labour, power, a specific input, output space) is currently limiting it
stories.so_that: I can act on the cause instead of guessing why output dropped — a past playtest verdict found critical warnings invisible, and a bare bool return today gives the player nothing to look at

acceptance_criteria.text: recipe_should_produce returns only a bare bool today; no bottleneck identity is captured or stored anywhere in the production path. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — souls/goods_company.rs, recipe_should_produce bare bool]

ProductionState must record a bottleneck field naming the single lowest-value active factor (e.g. NoResources(item), NoPower, NoWorkers, NoPlaceForGoods) whenever currentRate0to1 < 1, updated on every factor re-evaluation. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield ProductionState.bottleneck]

Selecting a throttled or stalled building in the UI displays its current bottleneck reason in player-readable form (e.g. "blocked: no iron"), visible without opening a debug view. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield; audit notes no severity-tiered notification system exists, only a single-slot ErrorTooltip]

stories.title: Let a building request more input than its recipe strictly needs
stories.i_want: an enterprise's declared input requirement to be a separate, inflatable number from the recipe's true consumption rate
stories.so_that: the core loop — enterprises hoard inputs and inflate their requests — has something to inflate; today the requested amount is always item.amount, so there is nothing to see through

acceptance_criteria.text: Today Market::buy_until, called from recipe_init/recipe_act, always requests exactly item.amount — the literal recipe quantity — with no distinction between plan quota and honest requirement. [SUBSTRATE: PROVIDED (as the un-deceptive baseline) — market.rs:161-167, called from souls/goods_company.rs:23,47]

A building must be able to hold a reported requested quantity per input that is independently settable and can exceed the recipe's true per-cycle consumption. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield; this is the hoarding hook the audit names as the cleanest insertion point]

Market::buy_until (or its successor) requests the reported quantity, not the recipe's literal amount, when the two diverge — the enterprise actually receives and stockpiles the inflated amount if the market can supply it. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield; requires additive fields on BuyOrder per audit §4]

stories.title: Distinguish true consumption from reported request in the production ledger
stories.i_want: the sim to track, per building per cycle, both what was actually consumed by the recipe and what was requested/received from the market
stories.so_that: a gap between the two is a measurable, queryable fact rather than something only visible by reading source

acceptance_criteria.text: A building accumulates unconsumed surplus stock when received input exceeds what the recipe consumes per cycle, rather than the surplus being silently discarded or never arising (today request == consumption, so no surplus is possible). [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield]

The per-building surplus/hoard quantity for a given input is queryable (e.g. via a component or market inspection API) distinctly from the input's in-flight order quantity. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield]

stories.title: Let the planner detect a hoarding enterprise from observable state alone
stories.i_want: to compare a factory's requested/received input quantity against what it actually consumes and notice when they diverge
stories.so_that: hoarding is a discoverable gameplay fact — the emotional core of the design — not an invisible backend number

acceptance_criteria.text: Selecting a building shows, for at least one input, both the requested/received quantity and the recipe's true per-cycle consumption, or a derived surplus figure, in the same panel. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield UI, no existing panel exposes recipe consumption vs order quantity]

Given two otherwise-identical buildings of the same type, one with an honest requested quantity and one with an inflated requested quantity, the inflated one visibly accumulates a growing surplus stock over multiple production cycles while the honest one does not. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield, depends on AC from surplus-tracking story]

stories.title: Give every resource item physical handling metadata
stories.as_a: planner and the logistics/construction systems built on top of resources
stories.i_want: each resource to declare mass, volume, a storage class, and a transport class
stories.so_that: logistics can decide which vehicle/container/network can carry a given resource and storage buildings can reject incompatible goods

acceptance_criteria.text: Today ItemPrototype is exactly {base, id, optout_exttrade} — no mass, volume, storageClass, or transportClass field exists on any item. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — prototypes/src/prototypes/item.rs:8-12, whole schema]
Every item prototype must carry a numeric mass (t/unit) and volume (m³/unit) field, loadable from the Lua catalogue like other prototype fields. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield]

Every item prototype must carry a storageClass (aggregate | covered | liquid | cooled | open | special) and a transportClass (compatible vehicle/network kinds), and two resources with disjoint transportClass sets cannot both be loaded onto the same transport instance. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield; no storage/transport compatibility check exists anywhere in the codebase per audit]

Every item prototype must carry an optional containerClass (aluminium | bio | construction | plastic | steel | toxic | open) for items that ship in typed containers, matching container_big_{aluminium,bio,construction,plastic,steel,toxic} material classes; a container's material determines what it may legally carry. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield; spec/resources.md:67,86]

Every item prototype must carry a category field with exactly one of {raw, processed-material, construction, consumer-good, liquid, energy, waste}, distinct from and in addition to its tier field. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield; spec/resources.md:56]

A network-borne resource (electricity, heat) declares no vehicle-compatible transportClass, and a query for vehicle-transportable resources excludes it entirely — never merely returning a transport-class mismatch as it would for two ordinary physical goods. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield; spec/resources.md:125]

stories.title: Give every resource item an economic tier classification
stories.i_want: each resource to declare whether it is raw, intermediate, finished, or luxury
stories.so_that: planning priority and trade value can be driven by tier without reintroducing floating money-based worth

acceptance_criteria.text: Every item prototype must carry a tier field with exactly one of {raw, intermediate, finished, luxury}. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield, no such field exists in prototypes/src/prototypes/item.rs]

stories.title: Give perishable and hazardous items lifecycle metadata
stories.i_want: perishable goods (food, meat) to decay past a shelf life outside cold storage, and hazardous goods (uranium, some waste) to be flagged as such
stories.so_that: refrigerated logistics and radioactive handling are physically meaningful rather than cosmetic categories

acceptance_criteria.text: An item may optionally declare a shelfLife; when stored outside a storageClass=cooled bucket (or its equivalent) past shelfLife, its stored quantity is reduced or removed rather than persisting indefinitely. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield; no decay mechanism exists anywhere in the simulation crate per audit]

An item may optionally declare a hazardClass (e.g. radioactive, toxic); items with a hazardClass set are distinguishable at the prototype level from ordinary goods (for later systems — construction siting, waste routing — to query). [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield]

stories.title: Replace the inverted opt-out trade flag with an explicit tradeable declaration
stories.i_want: each resource to declare tradeable directly rather than the codebase reasoning about the negation of optout_exttrade everywhere it needs to know
stories.so_that: trade eligibility reads as a positive, unambiguous fact matching the spec's Resource.tradeable field

acceptance_criteria.text: Today the only trade-related field is optout_exttrade — the inverse of the spec's tradeable — and every caller must negate it to get the spec's semantics. [SUBSTRATE: PARTIAL — prototypes/src/prototypes/item.rs:8-12, optout_exttrade is the sole existing field]

A tradeable accessor (or renamed field) exists such that tradeable == !optout_exttrade for every existing item, verified against every entry in the current catalogue with no behavioural change to which items trade externally. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield naming/accessor, behaviour-preserving]

stories.title: Let recipes emit byproducts alongside their primary outputs
stories.i_want: a recipe to produce sewage, air/ground pollution, or solid waste (ash) as a side effect of its primary output
stories.so_that: production isn't clean — dirty chains have a physical consequence the player must route or absorb, not a free externality

acceptance_criteria.text: Today Recipe has only consumption/production fields; no byproducts, pollutionTier, or waste emission field exists anywhere in the recipe type. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — prototypes/src/types/recipe.rs, per audit §3]

A recipe may declare a byproducts list (e.g. sewage rate, ash quantity) that is emitted every production cycle alongside its primary outputs, using the same output mechanism (must go somewhere — a byproduct with no output-space capacity throttles the recipe exactly like a primary output would). [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield]
A recipe may declare a categorical pollutionTier (small | medium | high) distinct from any numeric byproduct, matching the confirmed W&R POLLUTION_* token shape. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield]

A recipe's sewage byproduct (declared via a numeric sewage rate) is routed through a network connection to downstream sewage infrastructure, distinct from the bucket-storage mechanism used for solid waste byproducts like ash — sewage never occupies an output-storage slot. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield; spec/production.md:92 ($CONNECTION_SEWAGE_OUTPUT)]

stories.title: Require waste to be physically stored and hauled, not vanish
stories.i_want: solid waste byproducts (e.g. ash) to occupy real output storage and require freight to clear, exactly like any other good
stories.so_that: waste follows the same nothing-teleports rule as every other resource in the economy

acceptance_criteria.text: A waste byproduct accumulates in the producing building's output storage and is subject to the same output-space backpressure gate as primary outputs — a full waste buffer halts the recipe exactly like a full goods buffer does. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield; depends on byproducts existing at all]

stories.title: Let machinery condition throttle production output
stories.i_want: a factory's equipment presence and condition to act as an independent production factor
stories.so_that: wear becomes a maintenance decision the player manages, not an invisible constant

acceptance_criteria.text: Today a recipe only tracks n_workers; no machinery/equipment presence or condition field exists on any building or recipe type. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — single n_workers tier only, per audit §3]

A recipe may declare workingVehiclesNeeded (or equivalent machinery requirement); f_machinery contributes multiplicatively to output_rate exactly as the other factors do, and missing equipment reduces or zeroes the rate. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield]

stories.title: Gate advanced recipes on skilled/educated labour separately from general labour
stories.i_want: some recipes to require a second, educated-labour tier (professorsNeeded) alongside ordinary workersNeeded
stories.so_that: high-tech production chains distinguish general staffing shortfall from a shortage of skilled labour specifically

acceptance_criteria.text: Today Recipe carries a single workforce tier (n_workers); no second skilled/educated labour field exists. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — single n_workers tier only, per audit §3]

A recipe may optionally declare professorsNeeded as a second labour requirement; a shortfall in skilled labour throttles output independently of (and multiplicatively with) the ordinary labour factor, and the bottleneck reason (per the legibility story) distinguishes the two. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield]

stories.title: Gate production below a required water purity threshold
stories.i_want: a recipe that requires a minimum water purity to be blocked outright when its water input falls below that threshold
stories.so_that: water quality reads as a distinct binary gate among the six named production factors, not folded invisibly into the generic multiplicative formula

acceptance_criteria.text: Today no waterQualityMin field, threshold check, or f_water_quality computation exists anywhere in the recipe or production types. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield; spec/production.md:119,143]

A Recipe may declare waterQualityMin (0..1); when the recipe's water input quality is below waterQualityMin, f_water_quality is 0 and the recipe is blocked outright (not merely throttled proportionally) regardless of every other factor's value. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield; spec/production.md:45,82]

When the recipe has no waterQualityMin declared, or the supplied water quality meets or exceeds it, f_water_quality is exactly 1 and contributes no penalty to the composed output_rate. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield; spec/production.md:14-27]

stories.title: Recompute production factors when a gating input changes, not only on a fixed tick
stories.i_want: a factory's production rate and bottleneck to update as soon as its labour, power, or input stock changes
stories.so_that: the player sees a stall or recovery promptly instead of waiting up to a full production-frequency period for the sim to notice

acceptance_criteria.text: Today no change-triggered re-evaluation exists; nothing in the codebase asserts factor recomputation is driven by anything other than the fixed medium-frequency production pass. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield; spec/production.md:131]

A change to a building's present-worker count, available power fraction, or an input's stock level triggers factor re-evaluation (and bottleneck field update) on the tick the change is observed, not only at the next fixed medium-frequency production pass boundary. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield; spec/production.md:131]

stories.title: Modulate renewable-connected recipes' output by weather and day/night cycle
stories.i_want: a recipe connected to wind or solar power to have its output rate scaled by current weather and time-of-day conditions
stories.so_that: renewable-dependent production is a legible physical factor rather than a constant rate regardless of conditions

acceptance_criteria.text: Today no field or mechanism ties any recipe's output rate to weather or day/night state; no renewable-connection flag exists on Recipe. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield; spec/production.md:37,59,107]

A recipe may declare a connectedToWind or connectedToSun flag; when set, its base_rate is scaled by a current wind-strength or sunlight-availability value (0..1) sourced from the weather/day-cycle system, in addition to the other multiplicative factors. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield; spec/production.md:59]

stories.title: Let extraction recipes' output drift downward over calendar time as the resource depletes
stories.i_want: a mine or field's base output rate to decline over in-game calendar time
stories.so_that: depletion/ageing is a physical consequence of continued extraction rather than an eternal constant rate

acceptance_criteria.text: Today no field or mechanism reduces a recipe's base_rate as calendar time elapses; base_rate is a static constant. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield; spec/production.md:60,107]

A recipe may declare a yearly depletion rate; over N in-game years of continuous operation with this flag set, the recipe's effective base_rate is strictly lower than at year 0, while a recipe without the flag holds a constant base_rate over the same period. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield; spec/production.md:60]

stories.title: Let recipes recover a fractional yield of material from waste inputs
stories.i_want: a recycling recipe to consume a waste class as an input and recover only a stated fraction of it as usable output
stories.so_that: recycling is the physical reverse of the waste-byproduct chain, not a free 1:1 conversion

acceptance_criteria.text: Today no recipe field represents consuming a waste class at a fractional recovery yield; waste can only be produced as a byproduct, never consumed and partially recovered. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield; spec/production.md:63,94]

A recycling recipe may declare a waste input class and a recovery yield fraction (0..1), e.g. waste_steel at 0.98 or waste_plastic at 0.9; consuming 100 units of the declared waste class at yield 0.98 produces exactly 98 units of recovered output, not 100. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield; spec/production.md:63 ($WASTE_EXTRACTION waste_steel 0.98)]

stories.title: Support storage buckets pinned to a single resource and consumer-demand buffer tiers
stories.i_want: a building's storage to support a bucket reserved for one named resource and separate consumer-demand buffer tiers
stories.so_that: import docks that only accept one commodity and shop demand buffers are representable, not just a generic storageClass bucket

acceptance_criteria.text: Today storage buckets are undifferentiated by class only; no bucket type exists that pins itself to a single named resource id or that models a tiered consumer-demand buffer. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield; spec/resources.md:84]

A building may declare an import bucket pinned to exactly one resource id and capacity; the bucket accepts only that resource and rejects any other, even one of a compatible storageClass. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield; spec/resources.md:84 ($STORAGE_IMPORT_SPECIAL)]

A shop building may declare one of four consumer-demand buffer tiers (basic | advanced | hotel | prison), each an independent capacity bucket distinct from ordinary import/export storage. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield; spec/resources.md:84 ($STORAGE_DEMAND_BASIC/_ADVANCED/_HOTEL/_PRISON)]

scenarios.title: Refinery-style recipe consumes one input and yields two co-products
preconditions: A recipe is defined with 1 input item and 2 output items, plus a nonzero duration

steps.action: Run the recipe to completion once with input fully supplied
expected: Both output items are added to the building's output storage in their declared quantities
The input item is consumed in its declared quantity

final_observables: Both co-products exist in storage after one completed cycle
Consumed input quantity matches the recipe's declared amount exactly
owning_story_titles: Verify recipes transform multiple inputs into multiple outputs over duration

scenarios.title: Mine produces raw ore with zero declared inputs
preconditions: A recipe is defined with an empty inputs list and one output

steps.action: Run the recipe with full labour and power available
expected: Production proceeds without any input-availability check ever being evaluated
Output is added to storage at the declared rate

final_observables: Output quantity matches base_rate with no input items consumed
owning_story_titles: Verify extraction buildings produce with no consumed inputs

scenarios.title: Full output warehouse halts a producing factory, then resumes when space clears
preconditions: A factory is actively producing
Its output storage bucket is filled to capacity

steps.action: Advance the sim while output storage stays full
expected: Production rate drops to 0
No further output is added past the storage cap

steps.action: Clear the output storage (simulate freight pickup)
expected: Production resumes automatically on a subsequent tick without manual intervention

final_observables: Output storage never exceeds capacity
Production resumes once space is available
owning_story_titles: Verify full output storage halts production (the cascade engine)

scenarios.title: Linear staffing factor understates the intended curve's penalty at partial staffing
preconditions: staffFrac = 0.5, worker efficiency e = 1.0

steps.action: Compute today's linear factor (staffFrac) and the target curve factor (2e − 200e/(staffFrac+100))
expected: The linear result (0.5) is strictly greater than the curve result
The curve result is the value the acceptance criteria require after the fix

final_observables: Linear model output ≠ curve model output at staffFrac=0.5, proving today's implementation does not yet match the spec
owning_story_titles: Scale output continuously with staffing fraction, not linearly

scenarios.title: Partial power availability throttles output instead of an all-or-nothing blackout
preconditions: A factory is fully staffed and fully supplied on inputs
Its power network delivers 50% of required electricity, not zero

steps.action: Advance the sim one production cycle under 50% power availability
expected: Output rate is reduced proportionally toward 50%, not left at full rate and not dropped to zero
The factory is not marked as blacked out

final_observables: Realized output is strictly between 0 and full rate under partial power — proving the gate is no longer binary
owning_story_titles: Throttle output continuously with available power instead of a binary blackout gate

scenarios.title: Scarcest of two under-supplied inputs sets the throttled rate
preconditions: A recipe has two inputs; input A is at 80% of required stock, input B is at 30%

steps.action: Compute f_inputs = min(available/required) across both inputs
expected: f_inputs equals 0.3 (input B's fraction), not 0.8, not an average of the two

owning_story_titles: Throttle output continuously with scarcest input stock instead of an all-or-nothing stall

scenarios.title: Two independently-deficient factors compound multiplicatively, not by minimum
preconditions: f_labour = 0.5 (understaffed)
f_power = 1.0 (full power)
f_inputs = 0.3 (scarce input)
all other factors = 1.0

steps.action: Compute output_rate = base_rate × f_labour × f_power × f_inputs × f_machinery × f_water_quality × f_output_space
expected: output_rate == base_rate × 0.5 × 0.3 == base_rate × 0.15
output_rate is NOT equal to base_rate × min(0.5, 1.0, 0.3) == base_rate × 0.3

final_observables: Composed rate equals the product of all factors (0.15×base_rate), distinguishing multiplicative composition from a min()-only composition
owning_story_titles: Combine all production factors multiplicatively so the scarcest factor wins

scenarios.title: Player inspects a stalled factory and sees which input is missing
preconditions: A factory is stalled because its steel input reached zero while labour and power remain fully available

steps.action: Player selects the stalled building in the UI
expected: A panel or overlay names the bottleneck as the specific missing input (steel), not a generic 'stopped' or 'idle' state

final_observables: The bottleneck reason shown to the player matches the actual limiting factor (NoResources(steel))
owning_story_titles: Surface the active bottleneck reason to the player

scenarios.title: An enterprise with an inflated request accumulates surplus stock a matched honest enterprise does not
preconditions: Two identical buildings of the same recipe type exist
Building A's declared request quantity for its input equals the recipe's true per-cycle consumption (honest)
Building B's declared request quantity for the same input is set to 2x the recipe's true per-cycle consumption (inflated)
The market has enough supply to fill both requests each cycle

steps.action: Advance the sim through several production cycles
expected: Building A's input stock oscillates near zero between deliveries (consumes what it requests)
Building B's input stock grows cycle over cycle, since it receives more than the recipe consumes

final_observables: Building B holds a strictly larger surplus of the input than Building A after N cycles, proving the requested/consumed gap is now mechanically real
owning_story_titles: Let a building request more input than its recipe strictly needs
Distinguish true consumption from reported request in the production ledger

scenarios.title: Player detects a hoarding enterprise from its inspection panel alone
preconditions: Building B (from the hoarding scenario above) has accumulated visible surplus stock over several cycles

steps.action: Player opens Building B's inspection panel
expected: The panel shows both the requested/received input quantity and the recipe's true consumption for at least one input
The two numbers visibly differ

steps.action: Player compares Building B's panel to Building A's (honest) panel
expected: Building A's requested and consumed figures match; Building B's do not

final_observables: The player can, from UI alone with no source access, identify which of the two buildings is hoarding
owning_story_titles: Let the planner detect a hoarding enterprise from observable state alone

scenarios.title: Steel and fuel resources declare incompatible transport classes
preconditions: Steel item prototype has transportClass = OPEN (flatbed)
Fuel item prototype has transportClass = OIL (tanker)

steps.action: Query whether steel and fuel share a compatible transportClass
expected: The compatibility check returns false — no shared transport class

steps.action: Attempt to load steel onto a tanker vehicle instance (transportClass = OIL)
expected: The load is rejected

final_observables: Steel cannot be assigned to OIL-class transport; the compatibility contract is enforced, not merely documented
owning_story_titles: Give every resource item physical handling metadata

scenarios.title: Meat left outside cold storage decays past its shelf life
preconditions: A meat item prototype declares shelfLife = N ticks and storageClass = cooled as its compatible class
A quantity of meat is stored in an uncooled (open) storage bucket

steps.action: Advance the sim past N ticks with meat continuously in uncooled storage
expected: The stored meat quantity decreases or is zeroed once shelfLife elapses

steps.action: Repeat with meat stored in a cooled bucket for the same duration
expected: The stored meat quantity is unaffected (or decays at a slower/no rate)

final_observables: Uncooled meat quantity after N+1 ticks is strictly less than cooled meat quantity under identical elapsed time
owning_story_titles: Give perishable and hazardous items lifecycle metadata

scenarios.title: A combustion recipe emits ash that fills its own output bucket and can halt the recipe
preconditions: A recipe declares a primary output plus a waste_ash byproduct
The building's ash output bucket has finite capacity and is nearly full

steps.action: Run the recipe to completion enough times to fill the ash bucket
expected: Ash accumulates in a dedicated output-space bucket, consuming capacity like any other output

steps.action: Attempt one more production cycle once the ash bucket is full
expected: The recipe halts (output-space backpressure applies to the byproduct exactly as it does to the primary output)

final_observables: Production is blocked by a full byproduct bucket even though the primary output has free space, proving byproducts are first-class outputs subject to the same physical rules
owning_story_titles: Let recipes emit byproducts alongside their primary outputs
Require waste to be physically stored and hauled, not vanish

scenarios.title: Cooled-class storage bucket rejects an incompatible open-class resource
preconditions: A storage bucket declares storageClass = cooled
An item prototype (e.g. steel) declares storageClass = open

steps.action: Attempt to place steel into the cooled-class bucket
expected: The placement is rejected — the bucket accepts only cooled-class resources

steps.action: Place a cooled-class resource (e.g. meat) into the same bucket
expected: The placement succeeds

final_observables: Steel is never accepted by the cooled bucket while a cooled-class resource is, proving storage-class compatibility is enforced independently of transport-class compatibility
owning_story_titles: Give every resource item physical handling metadata

scenarios.title: Electricity is never returned by a query for vehicle-transportable resources
preconditions: Electricity item prototype declares no vehicle-compatible transportClass (network-only)

steps.action: Query the logistics vehicle scheduler for resources eligible to be assigned to a truck/rail transport instance
expected: Electricity does not appear in the eligible set at all

steps.action: Attempt to directly assign electricity to a vehicle transport instance
expected: The assignment is rejected

final_observables: Electricity is categorically absent from vehicle-transportable resources, not merely incompatible with one specific transport class
owning_story_titles: Give every resource item physical handling metadata

scenarios.title: Sub-threshold water quality blocks the recipe outright despite full staffing and power
preconditions: A recipe declares waterQualityMin = 0.6
f_labour = 1.0 and f_power = 1.0
Supplied water quality = 0.4

steps.action: Compute f_water_quality and the composed output_rate
expected: f_water_quality == 0
output_rate == 0 regardless of f_labour and f_power both being 1.0

steps.action: Raise supplied water quality to 0.6 and recompute
expected: f_water_quality == 1
output_rate is no longer forced to 0 by the water-quality factor

final_observables: The recipe is blocked below the threshold and unblocked at or above it, proving water quality is a binary gate distinct from the continuous factors
owning_story_titles: Gate production below a required water purity threshold

scenarios.title: Bottleneck reason updates immediately when an input stock is depleted mid-cycle
preconditions: A factory is producing at full rate with all factors satisfied
Its input stock for one item drops to zero mid-tick, before the next fixed production pass boundary

steps.action: Advance the sim by a fraction of the production-frequency period after the stock change
expected: The factory's bottleneck field updates to name the depleted input before the next fixed production pass boundary is reached

final_observables: Bottleneck reason reflects the depleted input before the next scheduled production pass, proving recomputation is change-triggered, not only tick-scheduled
owning_story_titles: Recompute production factors when a gating input changes, not only on a fixed tick

scenarios.title: Recycling waste_steel at its confirmed 0.98 yield recovers 98 of 100 units consumed
preconditions: A recycling recipe declares waste input class = waste_steel with recovery yield = 0.98

steps.action: Run the recipe consuming exactly 100 units of waste_steel
expected: Recovered output quantity equals 98 units exactly, not 100

final_observables: Recovered output == input_quantity × yield (100 × 0.98 == 98)
owning_story_titles: Let recipes recover a fractional yield of material from waste inputs

scenarios.title: A professor shortfall throttles output multiplicatively alongside a simultaneous labour shortfall
preconditions: A recipe declares workersNeeded and professorsNeeded
workers present / workersNeeded staffing fraction yields f_labour = 0.8
professors present / professorsNeeded yields f_professors = 0.5
f_power = f_inputs = 1.0

steps.action: Compute the composed output_rate including f_professors as an independent multiplicative factor
expected: output_rate == base_rate × f_labour × f_professors == base_rate × 0.8 × 0.5 == base_rate × 0.4
output_rate is NOT equal to base_rate × min(f_labour, f_professors) == base_rate × 0.5

final_observables: Composed rate equals the product of the labour and professor factors (0.4×base_rate), proving professorsNeeded throttles independently and multiplicatively rather than by minimum
owning_story_titles: Gate advanced recipes on skilled/educated labour separately from general labour
